entries.name: mkdir
entries.doc: Creates a folder.

args.name: folder
args.doc: The name of the new folder. A path such as a.b creates b inside the folder a.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace a folder that already exists. Everything in it is removed.

entries.name: cd
entries.doc: Makes a folder the current folder. Names in commands and expressions are looked up there (language.md 7). It cannot be used in the body of a for.

args.name: folder
args.doc: The folder. `..` is the parent folder, and `root` is the top folder.

entries.name: rm
entries.doc: Removes an array, a variable, or a folder.

args.name: target
args.doc: The array, variable, or folder to remove.

options.name: recursive
options.doc: Also remove a folder that is not empty, with everything in it.

entries.name: mv
entries.doc: Moves or renames an array, a variable, or a folder.

args.name: target
args.doc: The array, variable, or folder to move.

args.name: destination
args.doc: The new name, as a path. A path such as a.b moves it into the folder a with the name b.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace an array, variable, or folder that already exists at the destination.

entries.name: source
entries.doc: Registers a folder on this computer as a source of data files, under a name. The first time, a folder picker opens, and the browser stores the access permission (spec.md 10). Running it again with the same name keeps the stored access, so commands from the history can run again. Sources are not names in folders.

creates.doc: The source, used with from= in load.

entries.name: load
entries.doc: Imports a data file. Each column becomes an array, or the whole table becomes one 2D array (layout). Settings that are not given are detected automatically (spec.md 10.1). How a file name or a column label that is not a valid name becomes a name is an open question (spec.md Section 15).

args.name: file
args.doc: The file name in the source folder. `*` matches any characters. Each matching file is loaded into its own folder, named after the file without its extension.

options.name: from
options.doc: The source folder that holds the file.

options.name: format
options.doc: The file format. csv is any delimited text table (comma, tab, semicolon, or whitespace, as given by sep). npy is the NumPy format.

options.name: layout
options.doc: How the table becomes arrays. columns: each column becomes a 1D array. matrix: the whole table becomes one 2D array, with the columns along dimension 1 (x) and the rows along dimension 2 (y).

options.name: header
options.doc: The number of header rows: 0 (none), 1 (column names), or 2 (column names, then units).

options.name: skip
options.doc: The number of metadata lines before the table. Comment lines are not counted (spec.md 10.1).

options.name: sep
options.doc: The delimiter between fields.

options.name: decimal
options.doc: The decimal separator of the numbers. comma is possible only when sep is not comma.

options.name: comment
options.doc: Lines that start with this text are comments, such as "#".

options.name: encoding
options.doc: The text encoding.

options.name: missing
options.doc: Fields with these texts are missing values (NaN), such as ["NA", "-"]. If left out, the markers in spec.md 10.1 are used. Empty fields are always missing.

options.name: names
options.doc: The names of the arrays: one per column, or one for a matrix. If left out, the header row or the file name gives them.

options.name: into
options.doc: The folder that receives the arrays. It is created if it does not exist. If left out, the current folder.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace arrays that already exist.

creates.doc: One array per column, named by names or by the header row. With layout=matrix, one 2D array, named by names or by the file name.
The folder given by into, if it does not exist. With `*` in the file name, also one folder per file inside it.

entries.name: setcoord
entries.doc: Sets evenly spaced coordinates for one dimension of an array.

options.name: dim
options.doc: The dimension.

options.name: start
options.doc: The coordinate of the first point.

options.name: step
options.doc: The distance between points.

options.name: unit
options.doc: The unit of the coordinates, such as "meV".

examples: setcoord model dim=x start=0 step=0.05 unit="meV"

entries.name: setunit
entries.doc: Sets the unit of the values of an array.

options.name: unit
options.doc: The unit, such as "counts". "" removes the unit.

entries.name: note
entries.doc: Sets the note of an array, a variable, or a folder. Imported arrays get a note with the source file and the import settings.

entries.name: graph
entries.doc: Creates a graph. Sizes are those of the plot area, the rectangle inside the axes (spec.md 8.1).

args.name: graph
args.doc: The name of the new graph.

options.name: width
options.doc: The width of the plot area.

options.name: height
options.doc: The height of the plot area.

options.name: font
options.doc: The font family.

options.name: fontsize
options.doc: The font size of axis labels.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace a graph that already exists.

examples: graph fig1 width=60mm height=45mm font="Arimo" fontsize=9pt

entries.name: plot
entries.doc: Adds an xy trace to a graph. A string array as x, or an array with dimension labels without vs, gives a category axis (spec.md 8.3.1).

args.name: x
args.doc: The x values. If left out, the coordinates of y.

options.name: as
options.doc: The name of the trace, as a string expression such as nameof(d). It must be a valid name (language.md 2.3). Defaults to the name of y.

options.name: label
options.doc: The text in the legend, in figlab text notation (spec.md 8.4). Defaults to the name of the trace.

options.name: style
options.doc: How the points are drawn.

options.name: marker
options.doc: The shape of the markers.

options.name: size
options.doc: The width of the markers, including the edge.

options.name: open
options.doc: Draw open markers, with an edge and no fill.

options.name: color
options.doc: The color of the lines and markers.

options.name: dash
options.doc: The type of the line.

options.name: yerr
options.doc: Error bars in y: ± this array, or ± this number for every point.

options.name: xerr
options.doc: Error bars in x: ± this array, or ± this number for every point.

options.name: xaxis
options.doc: The x axis of the trace.

options.name: yaxis
options.doc: The y axis of the trace.

options.name: legend
options.doc: Show the trace in the legend.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace a trace with the same name.

examples: plot fig1 norm vs energy style=markers marker=circle size=3pt
plot fig1 model style=line color=gray dash=dashed

entries.name: image
entries.doc: Adds a heatmap of a 2D array to a graph. Each value is drawn as a flat pixel centered on its coordinates. NaN pixels are not drawn.

options.name: as
options.doc: The name of the trace, as a string expression such as nameof(d). It must be a valid name (language.md 2.3). Defaults to the name of z.

options.name: label
options.doc: The text in the legend, in figlab text notation (spec.md 8.4). Defaults to the name of the trace.

options.name: colormap
options.doc: The color map.

options.name: range
options.doc: The values mapped to the ends of the color map. Values outside get the color of the nearer end.

options.name: scale
options.doc: How values are mapped to colors.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace a trace with the same name.

entries.name: colorbar
entries.doc: Shows the color map of an image trace next to the plot area.

options.name: label
options.doc: The label of the color bar.

entries.name: unplot
entries.doc: Removes a trace from a graph.

entries.name: style
entries.doc: Changes the style of a trace, or of some of its points. With an index, only those points change (spec.md 8.2).

args.name: trace
args.doc: The trace. An index such as norm[10] or norm[20..29] selects points.

options.name: marker
options.doc: The shape of the markers.

options.name: size
options.doc: The width of the markers, including the edge.

options.name: open
options.doc: Draw open markers, with an edge and no fill.

options.name: color
options.doc: The color of the lines and markers.

options.name: dash
options.doc: The type of the line.

options.name: visible
options.doc: Draw the trace. A hidden trace stays in the graph.

entries.name: axis
entries.doc: Sets an axis of a graph.

options.name: scale
options.doc: The scale. A category axis is chosen from the data (spec.md 8.3.1).

options.name: range
options.doc: The range of the axis. A range from a larger to a smaller value reverses the axis.

options.name: label
options.doc: The axis label, in figlab text notation (spec.md 8.4).

options.name: tickdir
options.doc: The direction of the ticks: into the plot area, out of it, both, or no ticks.

options.name: order
options.doc: The order of the categories on a category axis: as in the data, by name, by value, or as listed.

options.name: ticklabel_angle
options.doc: The angle of the tick labels, in degrees.

examples: axis fig1 bottom scale=log range=0.1..100 label="\it{E} (meV)"
axis fig1 left range=auto label="Intensity (arb. units)" tickdir=inward

entries.name: legend
entries.doc: Sets the legend of a graph.

options.name: position
options.doc: The corner of the plot area.

options.name: frame
options.doc: Draw a frame around the legend.

options.name: visible
options.doc: Show the legend.

entries.name: export
entries.doc: Writes a graph to a file. The format is chosen by the extension: .svg, .pdf, or .png. Only the graph settings are used, not the view state (spec.md 9.4).

args.name: file
args.doc: The file name. A computed name is written in parentheses (language.md 3.1).

options.name: dpi
options.doc: The resolution of a PNG file.

options.name: transparent
options.doc: Make the background of a PNG file transparent.

options.name: text_as_paths
options.doc: Write the text of an SVG file as paths.

entries.name: fit
entries.doc: Fits a model to data (spec.md 6.5). The results go into the folder given by into. If the fit does not converge, the results are still stored, converged is 0, and a warning is shown.

args.name: x
args.doc: The independent variable. If left out, the coordinates of y.

options.name: model
options.doc: A built-in model, or a user function with | and one input.

options.name: init
options.doc: Initial values of the parameters. Built-in models estimate the ones that are not given.

options.name: fix
options.doc: Parameters that are held fixed.

options.name: bounds
options.doc: Bounds of the parameters, as ranges such as tau=0..inf.

options.name: range
options.doc: The coordinate range of the points used for the fit.

options.name: points
options.doc: The range of point indices used for the fit.

options.name: sigma
options.doc: The standard deviation of each point, used as weights.

options.name: maxiter
options.doc: The maximum number of iterations.

options.name: into
options.doc: The folder that receives the results.

options.name: replace
options.doc: Replace a result folder that already exists.

contents.name: covar
contents.doc: The covariance matrix. Its dimension labels are the parameter names.

contents.name: curve
contents.doc: The model curve, with the same number of points as y.

contents.name: resid
contents.doc: The residuals. NaN outside the fit range.

contents.name: chisq_red
contents.doc: χ² divided by the degrees of freedom.

contents.name: converged
contents.doc: 1 if the fit converged, 0 if not.

examples: fit intensity vs energy model=gauss into=fit1
fit decay vs time model=expdecay bounds=(tau=0..inf) sigma=err into=fit3

entries.name: help
entries.doc: Shows the help of a command, a built-in function, a fit model, or a user function. Without a name, shows a list.

entries.name: exp
entries.doc: The exponential function. Works element by element on arrays.

returns.doc: e to the power x.

entries.name: ln
entries.doc: The natural logarithm. Works element by element on arrays.

returns.doc: The natural logarithm of x. NaN for x < 0.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.doc: The square root. Works element by element on arrays.

returns.doc: The square root of x. NaN for x < 0.

entries.name: sin
entries.doc: The sine of an angle in radians. Works element by element on arrays.

returns.doc: The sine of x.

entries.name: round
entries.doc: Rounds to the nearest integer. Halves round away from zero. Works element by element on arrays.

returns.doc: x rounded.

entries.name: trunc
entries.doc: Drops the fractional part. Works element by element on arrays.

returns.doc: x rounded toward zero.

entries.name: max
entries.doc: The largest value of an array. NaN values are ignored. If all values are NaN, the result is NaN.

returns.doc: The largest value.

entries.name: ramp
entries.doc: Makes a 1D array whose values equal its coordinates: start, start + step, and so on.

args.name: unit
args.doc: The unit of the values and the coordinates.

returns.doc: The new array.

entries.name: sum
entries.doc: The sum of the values of an array. NaN values are ignored. The values are added in index order, so the result is the same on every platform (language.md 10.2).

returns.doc: The sum.

entries.name: zeros
entries.doc: Makes an array filled with 0.

args.name: n
args.doc: The number of points along dimension 1.

args.name: m
args.doc: The number of points along dimension 2, for a 2D array.

returns.doc: The new array, without coordinates.

entries.name: fill
entries.doc: Makes an array filled with one value.

args.name: n
args.doc: The number of points along dimension 1.

args.name: m
args.doc: The number of points along dimension 2, for a 2D array.

returns.doc: The new array, without coordinates.

entries.name: repeat
entries.doc: Repeats a 1D array along a new dimension 2, to align shapes explicitly (language.md 4.3).

args.name: m
args.doc: The number of copies along dimension 2.

returns.doc: A 2D array whose m columns along dimension 2 are copies of w. It keeps the coordinates of w along dimension 1.

entries.name: values
entries.doc: The values of an array without its coordinates.

returns.doc: A copy of w whose coordinates are not set.

entries.name: xvalues
entries.doc: The coordinates of dimension 1 (x), as an array.

returns.doc: An array of the same shape as w.

entries.name: yvalues
entries.doc: The coordinates of dimension 2 (y), as an array.

args.name: w
args.doc: The array. It must have at least 2 dimensions.

returns.doc: An array of the same shape as w.

entries.name: index
entries.doc: The point indices of dimension 1, as an array.

returns.doc: An array of the same shape as w, with values 0, 1, 2, …

entries.name: histogram
entries.doc: Counts the values of an array in bins of equal width.

returns.doc: The counts. The coordinates are the centers of the bins.

entries.name: count
entries.doc: Counts how often each string appears in a string array.

returns.doc: The counts, with the categories as dimension labels, in order of appearance (spec.md 8.3.1).

entries.name: str
entries.doc: Converts a number to a string.

returns.doc: The shortest text that gives the same number.

entries.name: num
entries.doc: Converts a string to a number.

returns.doc: The number. An error if the text is not a number.

entries.name: nameof
entries.doc: The name of a folder or an array, for example of a loop variable.

returns.doc: The name, without the path.

entries.name: folders
entries.doc: The direct subfolders of a folder, in name order. A for loop can iterate over them.

returns.doc: The subfolders.

entries.name: arrays
entries.doc: The arrays directly in a folder, in name order. A for loop can iterate over them.

returns.doc: The arrays.

entries.name: voigtpeak
entries.doc: The Voigt function, normalized to 1 at its center. It equals the Gaussian exp(-(x/wg)^2) as wl goes to 0, and the Lorentzian 1/(1 + (x/wl)^2) as wg goes to 0. Works element by element on arrays.

args.name: wg
args.doc: The width of the Gaussian component, as w in gauss.

args.name: wl
args.doc: The half width at half maximum of the Lorentzian component.

returns.doc: The value of the peak at x.

entries.name: line
entries.doc: Straight line.

entries.name: poly2
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 2.

entries.name: poly3
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 3.

entries.name: poly4
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 4.

entries.name: poly5
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 5.

entries.name: poly6
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 6.

entries.name: poly7
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 7.

entries.name: poly8
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 8.

entries.name: poly9
entries.doc: Polynomial of degree 9.

entries.name: gauss
entries.doc: Gaussian peak on a constant baseline.
entries.guess: y0: median of the points at both ends. a: maximum minus y0. x0: position of the maximum. w: from the full width at half maximum.
examples: fit intensity vs energy model=gauss into=fit1

entries.name: lor
entries.doc: Lorentzian peak on a constant baseline.

entries.name: voigt
entries.doc: Voigt peak on a constant baseline: a Gaussian and a Lorentzian combined.

params.name: wg
params.doc: Width of the Gaussian component, as w in gauss.

params.name: wl
params.doc: Half width at half maximum of the Lorentzian component.

entries.name: expdecay
entries.doc: Exponential decay on a constant baseline.

entries.name: dblexp
entries.doc: Sum of two exponential decays on a constant baseline.

params.name: tau1
params.doc: Time constant of the first component.

params.name: tau2
params.doc: Time constant of the second component.

entries.name: power
entries.doc: Power law on a constant baseline.

entries.name: sine
entries.doc: Sine wave on a constant baseline.

entries.name: sigmoid
entries.doc: Logistic step on a constant baseline.

entries.name: lognormal
entries.doc: Log-normal peak on a constant baseline. Only for x > 0.
